page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a large 50 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 131 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between compute-heavy and memory-bound workloads. The CPU performance is relatively modest, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core results falling into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show weak performance. However, memory subsystem benchmarks are more robust; memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks (365.1 GB/sec) and large uncached blocks (42.29 GB/sec read, 30.27 GB/sec write) place in the middle 50% tier. Passmark memory and database operations also achieve average ratings, and Redis SET operations perform steadily at 6.16 million operations per second.

Given the high memory density relative to compute power, the E8s_v3 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial RAM but do not demand high-frequency CPU performance. The trade-off is apparent in its weak computational and web-serving throughput, alongside poor text generation speeds for larger models. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and moderate enterprise applications that benefit from Premium Storage capabilities rather than raw compute-heavy processing or large-scale LLM inference.
